questions.q: Who came to Ezekiel and why did they come?
questions.a: The elders of Israel came to Ezekiel to inquire of Yahweh.

questions.q: What was Yahweh’s response to those who came to Ezekiel?
questions.a: Yahweh said that he would not be inquired of by the elders of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh command Ezekiel to make the elders know?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded Ezekiel to make them know the abominations of their fathers.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell the people of Israel about himself when he chose them in Egypt?
questions.a: Yahweh told them that he was Yahweh, their God.

questions.q: What did Yahweh swear he would do for Israel when they were in the land of Egypt?
questions.a: Yahweh swore that he would bring them into a land flowing with milk and honey.

questions.q: What command did Yahweh give the people of Israel in the land of Egypt?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded the people to throw away their idols of Egypt.

questions.q: How did the people of Israel respond to Yahweh’s command?
questions.a: The people rebelled against Yahweh and were unwilling to listen.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh say he acted to bring the people of Israel out of the land of Egypt?
questions.a: Yahweh said he acted for his name’s sake so that it would not be profaned in the eyes of the nations.

questions.q: Where did Yahweh bring the people of Israel after he brought them out of Egypt?
questions.a: Yahweh brought them to the wilderness.

questions.q: What did Yahweh give the people of Israel in the wilderness?
questions.a: Yahweh gave the people his statutes, judgments, and Sabbaths.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell the people they would be able to do if they obeyed his statutes and judgments?
questions.a: Yahweh told the people they would be able to live if they obeyed his statutes and judgments.

questions.q: How did the people of Israel respond to what Yahweh gave them in the wilderness?
questions.a: The people of Israel rebelled against Yahweh in the wilderness and rejected his statutes and judgments.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell the people they would be able to do if they obeyed his statutes and judgments?
questions.a: Yahweh told the people they would be able to live if they obeyed his statutes and judgments.

questions.q: What did Yahweh then swear he would not do for the people of Israel because they rejected his statutes and judgments?
questions.a: Yahweh then swore he would not bring them into the land he was going to give them.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say the people’s hearts were doing instead of following his statutes?
questions.a: Yahweh said their hearts were going after their idols.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do instead of destroying the people of Israel completely in the wilderness?
questions.a: Yahweh had pity on them and did not completely destroy them.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell the sons of Israel not to do?
questions.a: Yahweh told them not to walk in their fathers’ statutes, not to keep their judgments, and not to make themselves unclean with their fathers’ idols.

questions.q: What did Yahweh command the sons of Israel to do?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded them to walk in his statutes and to keep and do his judgments.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say his Sabbaths would be a sign of?
questions.a: Yahweh said the Sabbaths would be a sign between him and the people, so they would know that he is Yahweh their God.

questions.q: How did the sons and daughters of Israel respond when Yahweh commanded them to walk in his statutes and judgments?
questions.a: The sons and daughters of Israel rebelled against Yahweh and did not keep his statutes and judgments.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell the people they would be able to do if they obeyed his statutes and judgments?
questions.a: Yahweh told the people they would be able to live if they obeyed his statutes and judgments.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do instead of punishing the people right away, for the sake of his name?
questions.a: Yahweh held back his hand and did not punish them right away, for the sake of his name.

questions.q: What did Yahweh then swear to do to the sons and daughters of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh then swore to scatter them among the nations.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say the people did that led him to scatter them among the nations?
questions.a: Yahweh said the people did not keep his judgments, rejected his statutes, profaned his Sabbaths, and their hearts went after their fathers’ idols.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he gave the people because of their rebellion?
questions.a: Yahweh gave them statutes that were not good and judgments that they could not live by.

questions.q: What did Yahweh let the people do that made them unclean?
questions.a: Yahweh let them make themselves unclean by burning their firstborn children as sacrifices.

questions.q: How did the fathers of Israel blaspheme and betray Yahweh?
questions.a: The fathers of Israel blasphemed and betrayed Yahweh by offering sacrifices to idols on the high places.

questions.q: What did Yahweh accuse the people of Israel of doing, like their fathers did?
questions.a: Yahweh accused them of making themselves unclean and being unfaithful to him by worshiping detestable idols, like their fathers did.

questions.q: What were the people of Israel doing with their sons?
questions.a: The people of Israel were causing their sons to pass through the fire.

questions.q: What thought was in the minds of the people of Israel?
questions.a: The people of Israel were thinking they wanted to be like the other nations, worshiping wood and stone.

questions.q: How did Yahweh swear he would rule over the people of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh swore he would rule over them with a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and poured out wrath.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do to the people of Israel in order to judge them face to face?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would gather the people of Israel out of the countries where they were scattered into the wilderness of the peoples.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say about how he would judge the people of Israel, compared to their fathers?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would judge them just as he judged their fathers in the wilderness near the land of Egypt.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do to bring the people into the covenant?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would count each one of them, like sheep passing under a shepherd’s staff, and require them to honor the covenant.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would purge from among the people of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would purge the rebellious and transgressing ones from among the people of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say the people of Israel would no longer be allowed to do?
questions.a: Yahweh said they would no longer be allowed to profane his holy name with their gifts and idols.

questions.q: After Yahweh gathered the house of Israel on his holy mountain, how would Israel treat Yahweh?
questions.a: After Yahweh gathered the house of Israel on his holy mountain, Israel would treat Yahweh as holy in the sight of the nations.

questions.q: When would the people of Israel know that Yahweh is Yahweh?
questions.a: They would know when Yahweh brought them to the land of Israel that he had sworn to give to their fathers.

questions.q: What would the house of Israel think of themselves as they called to mind their past evil ways?
questions.a: The house of Israel would hate themselves for all the evil actions they committed.

questions.q: How did Yahweh say he would act toward the house of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would act toward them for the sake of his name, not according to their evil ways.

questions.q: What declaration did Yahweh make against the forest of the Negev?
questions.a: Yahweh declared that he would kindle a fire that would burn every face from south to north.

questions.q: Who will see that Yahweh burned the forest of the Negev?
questions.a: All flesh will see that Yahweh has burned it.

questions.q: What were the people of Israel saying about Ezekiel?
questions.a: The people of Israel were saying Ezekiel was only a teller of proverbs.

commentary.text: The elders of Israel are reminded of the idolatry in Egypt. (Ezek. 20:1-9) In the wilderness. (Ezek. 20:10-26) In Canaan. (Ezek. 20:27-32) God promises to pardon and restore them. (Ezek. 20:33-44) Prophecy against Jerusalem. (Ezek. 20:45-49)

Ezek. 20:1-9. Those hearts are wretchedly hardened which ask God leave to go on in sin, and that even when suffering for it; see Ezek. 20:32. God is justly angry with those who are resolved to go on still in their trespasses. Cause the people to know the evil deeds of their fathers, that they may see how righteous it was with God to cut them off.

Ezek. 20:10-26. The history of Israel in the wilderness is referred to in the new Testament as well as in the Old, for warning. God did great things for them. He gave them the law, and revived the ancient keeping of the sabbath day. Sabbaths are privileges; they are signs of our being his people. If we do the duty of the day, we shall find, to our comfort, it is the Lord that makes us holy, that is, truly happy, here; and prepares us to be happy, that is, perfectly holy, hereafter. The Israelites rebelled, and were left to the judgments they brought upon themselves. God sometimes makes sin to be its own punishment, yet he is not the Author of sin: there needs no more to make men miserable, than to give them up to their own evil desires and passions.

Ezek. 20:27-32 The Jews persisted in rebellion after they settled in the land of Canaan. And these elders seem to have thought of uniting with the heathen. We make nothing by our profession if it be but a profession. There is nothing got by sinful compliances; and the carnal projects of hypocrites will stand them in no stead.

Ezek. 20:33-44 The wicked Israelites, notwithstanding they follow the sinful ways of other nations, shall not mingle with them in their prosperity, but shall be separated from them for destruction. There is no shaking off God's dominion; and those who will not yield to the power of his grace, shall sink under the power of his wrath. But not one of God's jewels shall be lost in the lumber of this world. He will bring the jews to the land of Israel again; and will give them true repentance. They will be overcome with his kindness: the more we know of God's holiness, the more we see the hateful nature of sin. Those who remain unaffected amidst means of grace, and would live without Christ, like the world around them, may be sure it is the way to destruction.

Ezek. 20:45-49 Judah and Jerusalem had been full of people, as a forest of trees, but empty of fruit. God's word prophesies against those who bring not forth the fruits of righteousness. When He will ruin a nation, who or what can save it? The plainest truths were as parables to the people. It is common for those who will not be wrought upon by the word, to blame it.
